negative_findings: No mechanism model beats an AR(last reported d_margin) + Easter benchmark out of sample after multiple-testing control: 0 of 168 Clark-West tests survive BY. Cost-index, raw-material and gap DL models have negative out-of-sample R² at h=0-4 (-0.07 to -0.3), and multi-variable DLs overfit badly (R² as low as -3.8). The mechanisms are strong but mostly coincident (lags 0-2).

The unit-weight price-cost gap (food CPI minus raw-material inflation, equal and opposite coefficients at every lag) is rejected in all 16 specifications (p<=0.02, mostly <1e-4). Long-run homogeneity cannot be rejected in 13/16, but the lag sums are imprecise.

Energy (Nordic electricity, EU gas, Brent in NOK) has no margin effect once raw materials and packaging are controlled (multi-cost block p=0.74 full, 0.12 ex). The large full-sample screening significance of gas and electricity comes from 2021-23 only and disappears ex-episode.
Food-manufacturing PPI is not a usable cost proxy outside 2021-23. Ex-episode its sign flips positive (+1.2pp per 10% at lag 12): it behaves like the manufacturers' own selling price.
Global FAO and World Bank food indices (USD, EUR, NOK, SEK or local currency) are weaker margin predictors than the EU agri basket and EU packaging. FAO's p_BY is >=0.07 in both samples.

Real wage growth does not lead or explain Orkla volumes outside 2022-23. Full-sample vol_proxy t=0.6; ex-episode it is negative (coincident t=-1.5, real-time h=0 t=-3.7). The lead/lag profile has no significant positive lead at 1-4 quarters. The 2022-26 co-movement (corr 0.72 at lag 1) is one episode.

Consumer confidence (level), unemployment (level and change), retail food volumes, the policy rate and the saving rate have no robust full-sample relation with implied volume (|t|<2.3; confidence is negative ex-episode and in the joint model).

Cross-border shopping (Norwegian same-day trips, old survey) and SEK/NOK have no effect on Orkla volume or Norwegian grocery volumes once the 2020-22 border closures are blanked (1 of 12 lag tests p=0.01, none after BY). Unblanked, the series gives spurious p~1e-30 from COVID leverage.
EUR/NOK and the Orkla-weighted currency vs EUR have no margin effect once FAO USD commodity prices are controlled.

Management-cited volume weakness (46 quarters) is unrelated to macro volume indicators (AUC 0.36-0.53 for retail volumes, real wages, confidence, relative prices). It is largely idiosyncratic (Bakers 2010-11, Rieber 2013-14, destocking, campaigns, Czech ERP), though it matches the implied volume proxy (-3.5pp vs 0).
A plain 'input costs up' mention (64% of quarters) does not discriminate margin outcomes (-0.2pp, n.s.); only 'price increases lag costs' (-1.29pp) and 'costs stable or lower' (+0.74pp) do.

Post-2008 ex-episode, short-lag (0-6) raw-material effects on margins are small and insignificant (-0.15pp per 10% at lag 2). Outside 2007-08 and 2021-23, cost shocks are largely absorbed within the quarter under the Nordic definitions.
key_numbers: Margin level response to a permanent +10% raw-material shock (local ccy, K12 cubic PDL): trough -0.67pp at lag 3 (full) / -0.35pp at lag 2 (ex 2021Q3-23Q4); ex-episode half recovered by lag 5 (90% 2-11), zero by lag 6-7
Calibrated cost index +10%: trough -1.09pp (full) / -0.61pp (ex) at lag 2-3, vs a static no-pass-through accounting hit of -7pp (realised hit about 9-16%)
EU packaging PPI +10%: margin -1.6 to -1.9pp at lag 3. Rule: +10pp avg over lags 0-2 gives -1.5pp d_margin (full, t=-6.3) / -1.8pp (ex, t=-2.5)

Price-cost gap rule: +10pp in (food CPI ex VAT - calibrated cost index), avg lags 0-2, gives +0.84pp (full, p=0.001) / +0.63pp (ex, p=0.03) d_margin; best ex-episode gap weight on raw materials 0.26-0.34 (= cost share)
Cost acceleration (avg lags 0-3 minus avg lags 4-7 of the cost index): +10pp gives -0.62pp (full) / -0.48pp (ex) d_margin
Asymmetry: +10pp raw-material inflation gives -1.06pp within 1-2q; -10pp gives about 0 for 3q then +0.5pp (full) / +1.1pp (ex) by lag 6; profile equality p=1.4e-6 / 3.5e-5
FX: 10% SEK depreciation vs EUR gives about -0.4 to -0.8pp at lag 0-1, recovered within about 4q; Orkla-weighted currency vs USD 10% weaker gives -0.72pp after 6q (full, p=0.007), -0.29pp (ex)
Wages: 1pp faster wage growth gives -0.22pp margin by lag 2 (ex, p=0.06), about labour's ~20% revenue share

Price formation: 12-quarter pass-through of raw materials into food PPI 0.62 (full) / 0.31 (ex), half reached by lag 2-3; into food CPI ex VAT 0.56 / 0.28, half by lag 4-5; calibrated cost index into PPI 0.96 / CPI 0.88 (full)

Orkla price component 2022Q2-26Q2 = -0.23 + 0.97 x Orkla-weighted food CPI ex VAT (R² 0.85); Nordic CPI ex VAT R² 0.91; food PPI lagged 1q R² 0.90 (slope 0.77); cumulative Orkla price increase = 79-95% of CPI ex VAT (by calendar quarter)
Organic growth sensitivity to food CPI ex VAT: 0.62 (se 0.07) same quarter, 0.75 sum over lags 0-3 (full); 0.59 / 0.73 ex-episode
Implied volume proxy (og - food CPI ex VAT) vs reported volume/mix 2022-26: corr 0.83 (0.90 excl. 2025), slope 0.79
Relative food inflation (food CPI ex VAT - CPI): -0.84pp volume per 1pp (full, t=-4.9), -0.62pp (ex), -0.39pp real-time h=1

Episodes: margin trough 0-2q after the raw-material inflation peak (2007: 3q before); y/y margin back to >=0 0-4q after the peak; PPI peaks +0-2q, CPI ex VAT +2-3q, Orkla price +4q (2021-23: raw materials peak 2022Q2 +33%, margin trough 2022Q3 -3.0pp, recovery 2023Q2, Orkla price peak 2023Q2 16.3%)

Text: 22 regex themes on 102 notes, 17 manual corrections, kappa 0.86 (input-cost pressure) and >=0.93 for every other theme; 'price increases lag costs' quarters have raw-material inflation 12.6% vs 1.3% and d_margin -1.06 vs +0.23pp; management cost mentions align best with FAO local-ccy inflation 2q earlier (AUC 0.77)
Real time: best d_margin nowcast is EUR/SEK DL at h=0, out-of-sample R² vs AR +0.06/+0.09 (Clark-West p=0.011/0.002); AR+Easter benchmark R² vs prevailing mean 0.27 at h=0

Multiple testing: 1,097 tests in 21 families; 421 raw p<0.05; 199 BY<0.05 within family; 175 Holm<0.05 within family; 179 BY<0.05 across all tests; 0/168 real-time Clark-West tests survive BY; cost-candidate screen 64 tests (10 survive BY full sample, 4 ex-episode)
caveats: findings.md was NOT written: the harness blocks report files from subagents. The findings are in this output; all scripts, CSVs and PNGs are in /home/user/nordic-quality-rank/research/orkla_foods/analysis/mechanism/. No files under data/ or common.py were changed; nothing was committed.

Full-sample cost results rest on two episodes: 2007-08 (definition A, incl. CEE, Russia and ingredients) and 2021-23. Ex-episode magnitudes are about half and short-lag effects are imprecise in post-2008 ex-episode data.

Macro proxies are not Orkla's cost basket: the calibrated weights (raw materials 0.40, packaging 0.08, energy 0.02 x 0.25, wages 0.20) are assumptions. Spot FAO/EU prices vs contract and hedged buying and regulated Nordic agricultural prices attenuate coefficients. The 'about 15% of the static hit' figure blends true pass-through with attenuation.

The implied volume proxy assumes price pass-through of 1. This holds in 2022-26 (slope 0.97) but the level ratio is 0.79-0.95 and 2025 departs from it (food CPI about 4% vs Orkla price about 1%, driven by non-Orkla categories). Before 2022, the negative proxy vs food-inflation relation partly reflects incomplete price pass-through, not volume.

The 2022Q2-2026Q2 price/volume validation has n=17 and one cycle. Drivers there (confidence, real income, real wages, relative prices, retail volumes) are collinear and cannot be separated. Conservative small-sample p-values (max of HAC-t and OLS-t) were used.

HAC with about 100 overlapping y/y observations: unrestricted 7-lag chi² Wald tests over-reject, so F reference distributions plus PDL/ridge restrictions were used. Dropping 2021Q3-23Q4 creates a gap that C.nw_ols treats as contiguous (minor).
The 12-lag specification goes beyond the brief's lags 0-6. It was needed because margin recovery takes 5-7+ quarters. Lag 0-6 results are reported throughout as well.

M&A, definition and distribution-agreement effects (Bakers 2012, Rieber 2013-14, Hamé 2016-17, Tropicana/PepsiCo 2015-16, India 2014-22, Sweden ERP 2021) are noise in d_margin and og; event dummies are a robustness check only.

Latest-vintage macro data; geographic weights come from annual reports published after year end. The real-time evaluation handles publication lags, not revisions. The COVID dummy is excluded from real-time models.
The text themes come from paraphrased drivers_note texts, not full reports. The circular-shift permutation p-value has a floor of about 0.01, so BY is also reported on HAC p-values (p_BY_family_hac).
Cross-border shopping (old survey s1) is blanked for 2020Q1-2022Q4 (border closures); unblanked it gives spurious p~1e-30.

common.py: (1) nw_ols does not drop regressors that are constant within a subsample (e.g. def_A after 2008, india), giving rank-deficient designs and SingularMatrixWarning; worked around locally in 02_organic.ols() and mech_utils.fit_dl. (2) Subsamples via NaN make HAC treat non-consecutive quarters as adjacent. (3) load_targets d_og_r4 differences og_r4 across definition breaks without a flag (not used here).
